title: Shish kebab
subtitle: Grilled marinated lamb on skewers
excerpt: Shish kebab is cubed lamb marinated in olive oil, onion, and spices, then grilled on skewers over high heat until charred on the outside and pink within. The key is the marinade time and the heat: lamb needs both to develop flavour and stay juicy.
sourceNotes: Claudia Roden, A Book of Middle Eastern Food (1968). Shish kebab documented as one of the definitive grilled lamb dishes across Turkey, Lebanon, and the wider Levant. Paula Wolfert, The Cooking of the Eastern Mediterranean (1994). Marinade technique and cut preferences discussed in detail.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Marinate the lamb the night before for the best flavour. Keep covered in the fridge.
recipe.temperatureNote: Cook on the highest heat your grill or griddle can reach.

content.text: Shish kebab is marinated cubed lamb cooked quickly on skewers over fierce heat. The marinade is simple: olive oil, grated onion, paprika, and a little allspice. The lamb is threaded loosely on skewers so the heat can reach the meat on all sides, and cooked for eight to twelve minutes so it stays pink in the centre. Serve with pitta, yoghurt, and tomatoes.
You need metal or pre-soaked wooden skewers. A griddle pan or a very hot grill both work well.

Put the grated {{onion}} into a bowl. Add {{extra-virgin-olive-oil}}, {{paprika-sweet}}, {{allspice}}, {{cumin-ground}}, {{black-pepper}}, and {{sea-salt-fine}}. Squeeze in juice from {{lemon}} and stir to combine.
Add {{lamb-leg}} cubes and toss to coat thoroughly. Cover and refrigerate for at least two hours, or overnight for the best flavour.
Take the lamb out of the fridge 30 minutes before cooking. Heat a griddle pan or grill to the highest setting. Thread the lamb onto skewers, leaving a small gap between pieces.

Cook the skewers for three to four minutes per side, turning twice, until nicely charred outside and still pink within. The total cooking time should be eight to twelve minutes depending on the size of the cubes.
Rest for five minutes before serving. Serve on warm {{pitta-bread}} with {{plain-yoghurt}}, {{tomato}} halves, and a dusting of {{sumac}} if using.

items.symptom: The lamb is dry and tough
items.fix: Lamb leg should be cubed at 3 cm minimum. Cook to an internal temperature of 65 degrees for medium. Pull off the heat before it looks completely done.

items.cause: Pan not hot enough or meat is too wet from the marinade
items.fix: Pat the lamb briefly with kitchen paper before threading. The grill must be smoking hot before the meat goes on.
Soak wooden skewers in cold water for 30 minutes before threading. Metal skewers avoid this entirely.

items.symptom: The pieces are falling off the skewer
items.cause: Cut too large or threaded loosely
items.fix: Thread each cube through the centre and push the pieces slightly together on the skewer. Turn carefully with tongs rather than by the skewer handle.

content.text: Shish kebab (from the Turkish sis and kebap, meaning skewer and roasted meat) is one of the oldest forms of cooked food in the Middle East. The technique of grilling small pieces of meat on a skewer over open fire predates written records. In Turkey it is considered a separate tradition from the kofte-style minced meat kebab; in Lebanon and Syria it sits alongside grilled chicken and kofte on the restaurant grid as the standard charcoal offering. At home in the Levant it is a summer barbecue staple. The marinade is deliberately simple so the quality of the lamb speaks for itself.
